articles.title: CJGJ Ejected for Spitting at Brock Bowers, Raiders Players in Video, Bills DB Apologizes to Team
articles.summary: Buffalo Bills safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson was ejected from Sunday's matchup against the Las Vegas Raiders in the second quarter after appearing to spit in the direction of Brock Bowers and other Las Vegas Raiders players.
articles.body:
Buffalo Bills safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson was ejected from Sunday's matchup against the Las Vegas Raiders in the second quarter after appearing to spit in the direction of Brock Bowers and other Las Vegas Raiders players.

CJGJ acknowledged after the game that he needs to do a better job of managing his emotions and that he let his teammates down. He said he apologized to the team and spoke with the coaching staff following the incident:

Gardner-Johnson, 28, is never far from controversy, so Sunday's ejection won't shock anybody. But it left the Bills without a defensive starter for the entire second half.

The NFL could decide to take further disciplinary action against Gardner-Johnson upon further review next week.

Last season, Philadelphia Eagles defensive tackle Jalen Carter was ejected before the first play of the team's season opener against the Dallas Cowboys for spitting in the direction of Dak Prescott.

The league ultimately ruled that because Carter did not play a down, he served his one-game suspension in Week 1 and was therefore eligible to play in Week 2.

articles.title: Caleb Williams is back, and the Bears look dangerous
articles.summary: Williams returned with a flourish, throwing for 305 yards and reminding everyone just how good the Bears can be with him under center.
articles.body:
ATLANTA — The Bears are undoubtedly a better team with Caleb Williams in the lineup. Are they a great team? Perhaps. We'll have to wait until they play a game that's not as messy and chaos-ridden as the one they just blew through in Atlanta.

Williams was a ball of kinetic energy before, during and after the 31-23 victory in which he threw for 305 yards on 30-of-36 passing, with a touchdown and no interceptions. He jogged in place and threw air punches on the sideline, and he posed WWE-style after hitting Colston Loveland for the game's first touchdown. He even began his postgame remarks with a chipper "let's go, good to see you again" to the assembled media, and nobody thinks it's good to see the media.

Out the last three weeks with a hamstring injury suffered in Week 2 against the Vikings, Williams returned with a flourish, starting the game with 12 straight completions and posting 14 points before the Falcons had a single positive rushing yard.

"He was connecting everywhere. People were making plays all over the field," Rome Odunze said in an ecstatic Bears locker room after the game. "That's when our offense is really clicking. That's why we want to be in that flow-state mode. And we were in there today."

After opening with those two touchdown drives, Williams and the Bears slowed a bit, but still managed to double up Atlanta's time of possession, 40:08 to 19:52. Williams showed an uncanny ability to find the open man and keep drives going even in multiple third-and-long situations

"It's unique to be able to be as poised as he is in moments, get the play calling out, diagnose certain things, and then at the same time, be able to run 22 miles per hour, past 300-pound d-linemen," Odunze said. "It's incredible. That's what makes him, him. I'm super excited to have him back."

He wasn't the only one in the building charged up by Willams' return. Whether because of the easy proximity to the world's busiest airport, or the perpetually fragile loyalty of Atlanta fans, Mercedes-Benz Stadium and other Atlanta arenas often fill up with visiting fans from Pittsburgh, Dallas and — in dis case — Chicago.

Thousands of Bears fans — sporting orange, and black, and Ditka sweaters — welcomed Williams with roars loud enough to turn Mercedes-Benz Stadium into Soldier Field South. ("We love our fans," Falcons head coach Kevin Stefanski said afterward. "Our fans are so supportive, but we knew we would likely need to be on a silent count.")

The afternoon wasn't perfect. Chicago committed 12 often-sloppy penalties for 133 yards, more than 100 more than Atlanta. And after the Bears posted a 31-7 lead heading into the fourth quarter, after Chicago fans had yelled themselves hoarse shouting "Let's go Bears!" (with a little "Green Bay sucks" thrown in for seasoning) … well, the Falcons decided that they weren't quite done after all.

Michael Penix Jr. led Atlanta to two touchdowns within four minutes of game clock, and Williams wasn't able to kill the clock effectively enough. Atlanta actually got the ball back with 3:34 remaining down by just eight points, but a Penix fumble ended that threat easily enough.

Thing is, the game shouldn't have been that close. It was a reminder that even with Williams back in the lineup, the Bears still have some flaws to work out. This is, after all, largely the same team that got run out of Lambeau Field last week.

"[Sunday] was just one of those crossroads, if you will, because of what had happened the week before," Bears head coach Ben Johnson said after the game. "I told them after last week that I believe strongly in our coaching staff. I believe strongly in the locker room and with everybody that we have in the building. … It hadn't happened like that yet this year." (Well, it kind of did during that 59-point season opener, but you get what he's saying.)

Williams has dealt with doubts and questions his entire career, from his hesitation in the pocket to his personal sense of style to the way he handled his recent hamstring injury. But the simple truth is that he's on a trajectory toward becoming one of the NFL's top quarterbacks, and he has a receiving corps and a defense around him that can make Chicago one of the NFL's top teams. (The defense got a massive boost Sunday with the return of defensive back Kyler Gordon, who had three sacks and two forced fumbles, including the game-clincher on Penix.) If Williams can deliver at the level he's already hit on occasion, Chicago is in very, very good shape.

"He carries a chip on his shoulder, absolutely," Odunze said. "He plays with that fire. He plays with that passion. So when he goes out there, he's looking to prove some people wrong and prove himself right. And we feel that energy every single time."

articles.title: Colts sticking with QB Daniel Jones after latest turnover-filled loss to Titans: 'He's got to play better'
articles.summary: Daniel Jones threw two interceptions on Sunday in the Colts' loss to the previously winless Titans.
articles.body:
Daniel Jones isn't at risk of losing his starting job just yet. Indianapolis head coach Shane Steichen, after the Colts' 26-20 loss to the previously winless Tennessee Titans, confirmed that Jones will remain his starting quarterback moving forward despite his struggles this season.

"I think he knows he's got to play better," Steichen said. "I've gotta coach better. There's a lot of things, it's not on one guy. But we've got to do a lot of things better."

Jones, who made it back in time to start this fall after his Achilles injury late last season, has not played well in recent weeks. He went just 22-of-42 passing for 269 yards with a touchdown and threw two interceptions in Sunday's loss. Despite the Colts dominating the first half offensively — the unit racked up 232 yards while Indianapolis' defense held Tennessee to just 64 yards in the first two quarters — they had to settle for field goals twice despite being in prime position to find the end zone.

Jones' first interception came inside the red zone in the first quarter after he tried to force a pass to Josh Downs. Though in Jones' defense, Amani Hooker made a remarkable grab before falling out of bounds.

The second pick also came after a productive drive and resulted in a Titans field goal on the other end in the third quarter. The Titans tied the game on an eight-yard pass from Cam Ward to Carnell Tate in the fourth quarter, and then kicked a pair of field goals down the stretch to solidify their six-point win. Jones and the Colts went for it on fourth down on both drives between field goals and failed to convert each time.

Jones now has five interceptions to three touchdowns this season. The loss, Indianapolis' second straight, dropped it to 2-4 on the year. It also snapped a six-game win streak the Colts had over the Titans, and gave Tennessee head coach Robert Slaeh his first win running the team.

"I'm extremely disappointed," Steichen said, via The Athletic's James Boyd . "We've got a lot to fix, and we've gotta fix it in a hurry. Turnovers continue to be an issue, and we've got to handle that better … We've got a lot to clean up and we've got to fix it in a hurry."

Despite the Colts' rough start, Jones clearly still has the starting job under control. If Steichen were to bench him, that would presumably elevate Anthony Richardson Sr. to the starting role. Richardson, who the Colts selected with the No. 4 overall draft pick in 2023, has made only 15 starts over his first two seasons while dealing with various injuries. Jones won the starting job over him in training camp last year.

Many expected Richardson to be playing elsewhere this season after the Colts signed Jones to a two-year deal, but a trade never came together.

Jones has proven he is a capable starter in the league. He led the Colts to an 8-2 start last year, after all, and had them in great position to make the playoffs before his injury.

But so far this season, things have not gone well in Indianapolis.

articles.title: Kyle Juszczyk Slams CJGJ for Spitting on Him in 2025 After Bills DB's Ejection vs. Raiders
articles.summary: Buffalo Bills safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson was ejected during Sunday's matchup against the Las Vegas Raiders after spitting at Brock Bowers.
articles.body:
Buffalo Bills safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson was ejected during Sunday's matchup against the Las Vegas Raiders after spitting at Brock Bowers.

It didn't come as a major shock to San Francisco 49ers tight end Kyle Juszczyk.

"This is the least surprising thing ever," he wrote on social media while responding to a video of the incident. "CJGJ spit on me last year when we beat Chicago."

Players around the NFL don't seem particularly fond of CJGJ. In 2024, he was voted the league's most annoying player:

Coming into the 2026 campaign, Tim Graham of The Athletic noted that the volatile safety has been "fined 13 times for $194,924 over his seven NFL seasons."

That will likely increase significantly after this latest incident, which very well could include a suspension as well. The last two prominent spitting incidents involving Philadelphia Eagles defensive tackle Jalen Carter and Cincinnati Bengals wideout Ja'Marr Chase each resulted in one-game bans (Carter was ejected for spitting before his game and didn't receive additional punishment since he didn't technically play a game).

And despite the fact that he's undoubtedly talented—his 17-game averages of 73 tackles and four interceptions are solid marks for a free safety—he's also playing for his seventh different team in the past six seasons, a suggestion that perhaps his act wears thin inside of his own locker room.

"I want everybody to toe the line and, obviously, play with an edge," Buffalo head coach Joe Brady told reporters this week in response to CJGJ being penalized for unsportsmanlike conduct in last week's overtime win over the Los Angeles Rams and several other chippy moments. "But in all elements, we have to understand the situation, right? Allowing a 15-yard penalty when you've made a big stop, let's make sure that we're protecting the football team. I thought the guys did a good job around him of understanding the situation, but we can't put ourselves in those positions."

But yet again, CJGJ put his teammates in that position.

articles.title: Chiefs Beat Chargers, Box Score Stats, Highlights for Mahomes, Herbert, Kelce, Top Players
articles.summary: In an AFC West showdown, Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs came out on top, defeating Justin Herbert and the Los Angeles Chargers 22-6 at home while keeping their division rivals out of the end zone.
articles.body:
In an AFC West showdown, Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs came out on top, defeating Justin Herbert and the Los Angeles Chargers 22-6 at home while keeping their division rivals out of the end zone.

The Chiefs were 7.5-point favorites over the Chargers, per FanDuel Sportsbook , and improved to 5-0 with the win. The Chargers remained winless and dropped to 0-6 with the loss.

Kansas City held the Chargers to 259 total yards of offense while racking up 422 yards of their own, remaining one of three undefeated teams in the league alongside the Minnesota Vikings and San Francisco 49ers.

Herbert was sacked four times Sunday, bringing his season total to 21 through six games. He also went without a touchdown pass for the first time this season while throwing an interception that brought his season total to eight.

Kansas City scored on both of its first-quarter possessions, recording a field goal before Kenneth Walker III broke through for a a 33-yard touchdown.

Herbert and Mahomes traded interceptions on back-to-back possessions in the second quarter, but Mahomes bounced back, leading a drive that ended with Walker's second touchdown of the day.

A 23-second drive before halftime culminated in Harrison Butker nailing a 50-yard field goal to give Kansas City a 19-3 lead at the break.

Coming out of halftime, the Chargers held Kansas City scoreless and forced a fumble but managed just a field goal, trailing 19-6 entering the fourth quarter.

A fumble in the fourth quarter deflated any hopes of a comeback for Los Angeles, as Kansas City held on for the 16-point win.

The Chiefs will hit the road to face the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks next Sunday at 8:20 p.m. ET, while the Chargers head into a much-needed bye week.

articles.title: Updated 2027 NFL Draft Order After Week 6 Results, Who Could Chargers & Dolphins Take?
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Chargers have gone from potential playoff contender to winless and the projected No. 1 pick in the 2026 draft order in the span of six weeks.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Chargers have gone from potential playoff contender to winless and the projected No. 1 pick in the 2026 draft order in the span of six weeks.

Jim Harbaugh's team lost again on Sunday to the Kansas City Chiefs. The defeat combined with the Miami Dolphins' bye week and the Tennessee Titans' win over the Indianapolis Colts pushed the Chargers up to No. 1 as the only 0-6 team in the NFL.

The good news for the Chargers is that they don't need a quarterback in a draft class that is looking worse by the week at the position.

However, the Chargers do need a wide receiver and one of the best prospects in recent memory plays that position.

Ohio State's Jeremiah Smith might be the surest thing in the draft class based off seven weeks of performances in college football.

The silver lining to a bad Chargers season might be the ability to land Smith in April.

10. New York Jets (via Indianapolis 2-4)

Jeremiah Smith is looking more and more like the safest pick in the 2027 draft class.

The Ohio State wide receiver is 16 yards away from the 1,000-yard mark in mid-October.

Smith had an average 68-yard, one-touchdown performance in Ohio State's win over the Indiana Hoosiers on Saturday.

Entering the college football season, Smith was viewed as a top prospect along with quarterbacks, like Arch Manning and Dante Moore.

However, injuries and poor play from the majority of the draft-eligible quarterbacks opened the door for Smith to be the clear-cut No. 1 pick.

The Chargers could use some help for Justin Herbert. Smith would be the ideal partner for the veteran quarterback. He'd be an instant upgrade over Ladd McConkey and Quentin Johnston.

A lot of things have to be fixed for the Chargers to be a competitive team again, but if they don't figure things out in 2026, Smith could be waiting for them to restart the franchise's trajectory in 2027.

Darian Mensah might be the best quarterback prospect in the 2027 draft class.

The Miami Hurricanes signal-caller threw for 326 yards and three touchdowns in his team's double-overtime triumph over the Florida State Seminoles on Saturday.

Mensah's thrown for 1,764 yards and 18 touchdowns in his first season at Miami. He only has one interception, which he threw against FSU.

At the moment, Mensah stands out in a class where Arch Manning's disappointed and Dante Moore has been sidelined due to an injury.

C.J. Carr struggled in Notre Dame Fighting Irish's loss to the BYU Cougars on Saturday night and Drew Mestemaker has been good in some stretches for the Oklahoma State Cowboys.

The Dolphins should know a lot about Mensah with him playing in the same city. He might end up as the best fit the Dolphins if they'd like to move on from Malik Willis after one season.

Mensah could also be a good fit with the Tennessee Titans, if they want to move on from Cam Ward.

Miami and Tennessee are the most quarterback-needy teams in the top five of the current draft order. The New York Jets are an interesting franchise to watch as well in the quarterback conversation as the season goes on.

articles.title: Chiefs CB Christian Roland-Wallace ejected after throwing punch vs. Chargers
articles.summary: Roland-Wallace threw a punch in retaliation at Chargers guard Alex Harkey after he was shoved away.
articles.body:
Kansas City Chiefs cornerback Christian Roland-Wallace was ejected from Sunday's 22-6 win over the Los Angeles Chargers at the beginning of the fourth quarter for throwing a punch.

Following a 3-yard rush by Chargers running back Omarion Hampton, guard Alex Harkey finished off a block on Roland-Wallace by pushing him away from the pile after the play ended. That drew a penalty from officials.

Roland-Wallace then responded by turning around and throwing a punch at Harkey as he was down on his knees. That occurred within view of two officials who immediately ejected the cornerback from the game.

Harkey was penalized for unsportsmanlike conduct for the shove and both teams were called for offsetting penalties on the play. At the time, the Chargers trailed the Chiefs, 19-6.

Roland-Wallace appeared to get an interception off Justin Herbert early in the second quarter. But the play was negated with a roughing the passer penalty on defensive end Ashton Gillotte.

A reserve cornerback, Roland-Wallace came into Sunday's matchup with four total tackles. He is in his third season with Kansas City, signing as an undrafted free agent out of Arizona in 2024. In 32 career games, Roland-Wallace has 2 career interceptions, 72 tackles, 4 passes defended and 1 forced fumble.

Before being ejected, Roland-Wallace had 1 tackle for loss and 4 tackles overall in the Chiefs' win, which improved them to 5-0 this season. The Chargers dropped to 0-6, one of the NFL's two winless teams. (The 0-5 Miami Dolphins are on a bye this week.)

Patrick Mahomes completed 23 of 30 passes for 272 yards and 1 interception in Kansas City's win. Kenneth Walker III rushed for 128 yards and 2 TDs on 19 carries, and Xavier Worthy tallied 7 receptions for 73 yards.

For Los Angeles, Herbert threw for 204 yards and 1 INT, completing 22 of 37 passes. He was also the Chargers' leading rusher with 26 yards on 5 carries, which surely indicates the offense's lack of success against the Chiefs. Quentin Johnston caught a pass for 57 yards.

articles.title: Bills Beat Raiders, Box Score Stats, Highlights for Josh Allen, Cousins, Jeanty, Top Players
articles.summary: Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills charged into Sin City and defeated Kirk Cousins and the Las Vegas Raiders 33-30 on Sunday.
articles.body:
Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills charged into Sin City and defeated Kirk Cousins and the Las Vegas Raiders 33-30 on Sunday.

The Bills entered Allegiant Stadium as 5.5-point favorites over the Raiders, per FanDuel Sportsbook , and scored 20 second-half points to secure the road win.

The win was highlighted by an incredible touchdown flip pass from Allen in the third quarter, one that could go down as one of the season's best plays.

The Bills scored on their first three drives of the game, with Tyler Bass nailing field goals from 44 and 28 yards before Allen found wide receiver Khalil Shakir for a 9-yard touchdown.

Meanwhile, the Raiders' offense was also moving, scoring on three of its four first-half possessions.

Ashton Jeanty opened the scoring for Las Vegas with a short rushing touchdown before Matt Gay added two field goals, the second as time expired in the first half, to tie the game at 13-13 heading into the break.

The Bills came out of halftime without safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson, who was ejected for unsportsmanlike conduct with 15 seconds left in the first half after he appeared to spit toward a group of Raiders players.

A miscue by Las Vegas proved costly, as Cousins threw an interception that set up a 32-yard Buffalo drive capped by an Allen-to-Keon Coleman touchdown connection, giving the Bills a 23-13 lead after three quarters.

A field goal and a Cousins touchdown pass to Tre Tucker tied the game at 23-23 as Las Vegas went on a 10-0 scoring run to open the fourth quarter.

The Bills quickly responded with a 10-point run of their own, as James Cook III rushed for a touchdown and Buffalo added a field goal to regain a 33-30 lead.

Despite Cousins connecting with Tucker for a 44-yard touchdown pass following a 24-second drive, the Raiders' comeback attempt fell short when Buffalo recovered the ensuing onside kick to seal the win.

Las Vegas will host the Los Angeles Rams next Sunday at 4:25 p.m. ET, while the Bills head into a bye week.

articles.body:
A third of the NFL season is nearly in the books, and plenty of injuries along the way have undoubtedly shaken up fantasy managers' lineups. This is the time of the year that smart waiver-wire claims can be the difference between pulling ahead in your division or digging a hole that seems too big to climb out of.

This week's picks include a receiver who is continuing his positive trend of having more points each week than the previous one and a wideout who just returned from a Week 1 injury. In fact, all three of our selections this week are wideouts with major upside.

Points use PPR scoring. Scoring and rostered data via FantasyPros .

Week 6 stats: 4 rec, 107 rec yds, 1 rec TD, 20.7 pts

In last week's iteration of this round-up, we advised fantasy managers to grab Jaylin Noel off waivers after his 12.7-point day including five receptions for 41 yards and a receiving touchdown. It was his second double-digit outing in as many games.

Managers may have believed that Noel's fantasy value was touchdown-dependent, which would explain why he's still only rostered in 6% of leagues heading into Week 7.

However, Noel's 20-plus-point day on Sunday, his best game of the season, continues the pattern we're seeing: as offensive coordinator Nick Caley and head coach DeMeco Ryans give him opportunities, he's taking advantage of them, and thus earning more opportunities. His standout performance in the Texans' win over the Jaguars included hauling in a 50-yard pass.

Don't miss your chance to add him as a flex option moving forward.

Week 6 stats: 6 rec, 103 rec yds, 1 rec TD, 19.3 pts

Omar Cooper Jr. was returning from a four-game absence with an ankle injury in Week 6 against the Patriots, so it makes sense fantasy managers may have wanted to wait and see how he looked.

Well, there was certainly no snap count to worry about on Sunday, as Cooper led the Jets' wide receiver room in his return with a team-high six receptions on seven targets, more than 100 yards and a receiving touchdown to boot.

Given that Adonai Mitchell is sidelined with a finger injury, Cooper's upside is even more immediate. Managers should be sure to prioritize this claim ahead of Week 7.

Week 6 stats: 11 rec, 87 rec yds, 1 rec TD, 25.7 pts

"I love everything he's doing," Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy said about rookie wideout Germie Bernard Sunday, noting that the team has "put a lot on [Bernard's] plate." That was certainly the case in the Week 6 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, as Bernard saw a whopping 12 targets from Aaron Rodgers, bringing in 11 of them.

Bernard's 12 targets didn't lead the team—DK Metcalf did, with 15 targets—but Bernard was up there.

We know that when Rodgers trusts a receiver, he tends to look for him all game long, and there's reason to believe that's increasingly going to be the case with Bernard. "There comes a time when the confidence starts to match the potential," Rodgers said Sunday, noting that that time seems to have come for the rookie.

articles.title: Davante Adams leaves Rams' late loss to Cardinals due to apparent knee injury
articles.summary: Davante Adams pulled up awkwardly in the end zone and immediately reached for his left knee.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Rams lost wide receiver Davante Adams during the final stretch of their loss to the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday .

Adams, on the Rams' final drive of the contest, suddenly pulled up and started hopping in the back of the end zone. He reached for his left knee as play went the other way, and he eventually limped off the field to the sideline.

Adams did not return to the game. Further specifics of his injury are not yet known.

The Rams did end up scoring a touchdown on that drive. Matthew Stafford found tight end Colby Parkinson for a 6-yard score. But the Cardinals, with just 47 seconds left, made it all the way down the field to set up a game-winning, 43-yard field goal from Chad Ryland as time expired. They were aided by an unnecessary roughness penalty on Josh Wallace.

Adams finished with three catches for 39 yards and was targeted four times in the 18-16 loss. He has 441 yards and four touchdowns on 27 catches this season, his second with the Rams.

While it's unclear how long Adams will be sidelined, if at all, the injury comes amid a tough stretch for a team that many thought would run the table and win the Super Bowl entering the season.

The Rams fell to 2-4 with the loss, their second straight. The Cardinals are just 2-4, too, but they had lost four straight entering Sunday's contest at SoFi Stadium and have yet to win a game on their home field.

Losing Adams for any significant stretch will undoubtedly make it that much more difficult for Stafford and the Rams' offense to turn things around after this rough start.

articles.title: Patriots' A.J. Brown Says There's 'No Excuses' for Career-Worst Drops in Return from Injury
articles.summary: A.J. Brown dropped a career-high three passes during Sunday's 26-19 win over the New York Jets, a rough return to the field after the New England Patriots' wideout missed four games on injured reserve with a high-ankle sprain.
articles.body:
A.J. Brown dropped a career-high three passes during Sunday's 26-19 win over the New York Jets, a rough return to the field after the New England Patriots' wideout missed four games on injured reserve with a high-ankle sprain.

"My timing was off. I'm much better than what I put on display today. There's no excuses. I'll be better," Brown told reporters after the contest. "I expect myself to make each one of those plays. I'm more than capable of making those catches."

Brown was the team's big offseason addition but has played in parts of just two games, registering just six catches for 103 yards. But expectations remain high in New England regarding the star wideout.

"First of all, it was great to see him back out there. He looks cool in the huddle. So I'm looking forward to just growing, just building the connection," Drake Maye told reporters after Sunday's win. "I think there's some [on] me, [and] there's obviously some plays he wished he had back. But man, I was just [saying] in the locker room, 'You ain't got to worry about [No.] 1. He's a player in this league. He's going to be one of the best players on the field every time he steps on it.' I told him I'm going to keep coming his way, and I don't really think there's too much [else] to say about it. He's a great player. He's got great hands. He's got great releases, and he was open. I thought he looked good running around."

articles.title: Rams have a legitimate gripe with NFL officials, but their 2-4 record is the bigger problem
articles.summary: A questionable flag helped the Cardinals finish off the Rams, but a team built to chase a Super Bowl has plenty to answer for after dropping to 2-4.
articles.body: The Los Angeles Rams have another reason to complain about NFL officiating. They also have a 2-4 record after losing at home to an Arizona Cardinals team that entered Sunday with one win. I'd be a lot more concerned about the second part. Yes, a questionable personal foul helped Arizona get into position for the winning field goal in its 18-16 victory. Rams fans have every right to be frustrated, especially given what happened against Denver earlier this season. FORMER NFL QB SEAN SALISBURY WANTS OFFICIALS TO FACE POSTGAME QUESTIONS LIKE PLAYERS AND COACHES But this was supposed to be the NFL's superteam. The preseason Super Bowl favorite. A team built to win a championship right now. Instead, Los Angeles needed a touchdown in the final minute just to take the lead against the Cardinals. Then it couldn't get through the remaining 47 seconds. That's a problem that goes well beyond the officials. The Rams finally took the lead, then gave it right back Matthew Stafford's 6-yard touchdown pass to Colby Parkinson capped an 86-yard drive and tied the score 15-15 with 47 seconds remaining. But what should have been a routine go-ahead extra point was anything but. Rams kicker Blake Grupe had injured his knee tackling Devin Duvernay just over five minutes into the game and did not return, leaving punter Ethan Evans to attempt the crucial kick. RAMS KICKER BLAKE GRUPE KNOCKS HIMSELF OUT OF HIS DEBUT WITH A DISASTROUS TACKLE ATTEMPT He drilled it, and for a moment it looked like Los Angeles was going to escape with a win it probably didn't deserve. But one play, albeit a controversial one, was all Arizona needed to reach field-goal range. The Rams jumped offsides on the first snap of the Cardinals' possession, giving quarterback Jacoby Brissett a free play to take a shot down the field. He hit Jalen Brooks for 21 yards. Rams cornerback Josh Wallace was flagged for unnecessary roughness on the tackle, adding 15 yards and moving the Cardinals to the Los Angeles 29-yard line. FOX analyst Greg Olsen repeatedly insisted during the broadcast that Wallace's hit wasn't a foul. FOX rules analyst Mike Pereira also said there wasn't enough to warrant a personal foul. After three running plays, Chad Ryland hit a 43-yard field goal as time expired. It was Ryland's sixth field goal of the day. The questionable call certainly helped Arizona. But the Rams had already given Brissett a free play and allowed a 21-yard completion on a drive that began with 47 seconds remaining and the Cardinals out of timeouts. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Another questionable call, another loss Making the ending even more frustrating for Rams fans was the player involved. Wallace was flagged for pass interference against Denver, erasing an interception. Rams head coach Sean McVay later said the NFL acknowledged it was a mistake. Now Wallace and the Rams have another call to be angry about, and another loss in the standings. Look, saying a team should have played better doesn't excuse a questionable call that helps decide the game. The officials still have a job to do, regardless of what happened before the flag. But so do McVay, the Rams' offensive line and a defense that took the field with a lead and 47 seconds remaining. Los Angeles needed a last-minute touchdown to take the lead over a team that entered the red zone five times and failed to score a single touchdown. SEAN MCVAY IS 'SICK' ABOUT HIS OVERTIME CALL AS ANOTHER SUPER BOWL COACH PUBLICLY REGRETS END OF GAME DECISION Arizona's pass rush repeatedly disrupted the Rams' offense, keeping Stafford off-balance for most of the game. Now, credit to Stafford: He showed up with the game on the line and led his team on an 86-yard touchdown drive to take the lead. Still, the Rams had nine points through 59 minutes. That's a pretty big concern for a team led by Stafford with offensive weapons like Puka Nacua, Davante Adams and Kyren Williams. The upcoming schedule gives the Rams a chance to recover, with the Raiders, Chargers and Commanders up next. But after watching this performance, I'm not sure Los Angeles should be looking at anyone as an easy win. They're too talented to write off after six games. They're also 2-4, and the preseason hype isn't going to help them climb out of that hole. Neither is another explanation from the NFL about a flag.

articles.title: Sean McVay Rips Rams for Mistakes After Shocking Loss to Cardinals, 'Nothing Positive' From Game
articles.summary: Sean McVay didn't mince words after his team's 18-16 loss against the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday, a result that dropped the team to a surprising 2-4 on the season.
articles.body:
Sean McVay didn't mince words after his team's 18-16 loss against the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday, a result that dropped the team to a surprising 2-4 on the season.

"We won't win a game unless we figure out how to not beat ourselves," he told reporters. "Just so many unforced errors, so many things that are not in alignment with what we want to do, specifically on the offensive side of the ball. Give up a big return to start. Lose the kicker covering on that kickoff coverage and that comes out for a big gain. We didn't do enough. I thought out defense did enough to keep us in the game, but anytime we'd string a little bit of momentum we'd turn it over, take a negative, we jump offsides on a 4th-and-3 to put it to a 4th-and-8. We have a lot to look at ourselves on, and we have to go back to the drawing board and figure out how to improve."

The Rams managed just 286 yards of offense, had a turnover, failed to convert a two-point conversion after they opted not to kick the extra point after Blake Grupe was hurt and were 0-for-2 on fourth downs. They lost against a Cardinals team that didn't score a single touchdown but finished 6-of-6 on field goals.

The Rams were a trendy Super Bowl pick after a busy offseason that included the addition of superstar edge-rusher Myles Garrett and the return of Aaron Donald. Thus far, however, the Rams have pretty massively underachieved, even taking into account some issues with injuries.

Losing against a Cardinals team that came into Sunday with just one win was a pretty clear indicator that something has gone awry in Los Angeles.

articles.title: Cardinals send reeling Rams to 2-4 and in danger of missing the playoffs with late rally aided by controversial penalty
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Rams entered the season as favorites to win the Super Bowl. Through six weeks of the NFL season, they look like anything but after another to...
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Rams entered the season as favorites to win the Super Bowl. Through six weeks of the NFL season, they look like anything but, and are in danger of missing the playoffs.

The Rams dropped to 2-4 on Sunday with a stunning 18-16 loss to the Arizona Cardinals that drops them well out of the race in the NFC West, and leaves them with an uphill battle to get into wild-card contention.

Like the Rams' Week 3 loss to the Denver Broncos , this one was not without officiating controversy.

After trailing for most of the game, the Rams drove 86 yards on eight plays to secure a 16-15 lead with 47 seconds remaining in regulation. The Cardinals started their ensuing possession at their own 35-yard line following a touchback.

Should this have been unnecessary roughness?

A 21-yard pass from Jacoby Brissett to Jalen Brooks on the first play of the drive moved the ball across midfield, and a questionable unnecessary roughness penalty on the hit added 15 yards to the gain.

Rams cornerback Josh Wallace was in zone coverage on the play and waiting to make a hit on Brooks after the receiver leapt in the air to make the catch.

As Brooks landed, his helmet made grazing contact with Wallace's shoulder pad. Wallace leaned in to make the hit, but contact was minimal. The call of a personal foul was questionable at best.

That play and penalty set the Cardinals up with 1st-and-10 at the Los Angeles 29-yard line. It ultimately set Chad Ryland up for a 43-yard game-winning field goal as time expired.

It added up to another tough-luck loss for the Rams, but they didn't look good throughout Sunday's game. Afteward, head coach Sean McVay put the onus of the loss on his team, not the late call.

Sean McVay: 'There's nothing positive I can say'

"We won't win a game unless we figure out how not to beat ourselves," McVay told reporters. "Just so many unforced errors. … "There's nothing positive I can say about today."

He said this about the final Cardinals possession:

"Unfortunately on the very first play of the two-minute, we give up a big play, and they tack on the 15," McVay continued. "A good, humbling day. This is the challenge in sports."

An offense that entered Sunday leading the NFL in yards per game was ineffective against a Cardinals defense that entered the game ranked 26th in the league.

With left tackle Alaric Jackson suspended due to his postgame punch of Bradley Chubb last week, Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford was under pressure early and often, and the Rams struggled to gain any traction in the passing game until their late drive to take the 16-15 lead.

The Cardinals sacked Stafford three times and hit him five more. He was under consistent pressure even when he wasn't getting hit. The result was a Rams offense that managed just one touchdown and nine points through the game's first 59-plus minutes.

The Rams had 107 yards at halftime and finished with 286 for the game.

That final tally and Stafford's final stat line (25 of 33, 222 yards, 2 TDs, 0 INTs) were salvaged by the late 86-yard touchdown drive that featured completions of 16 and 43 yards from Stafford to Puka Nacua. Tight end Colby Parkinson stretched for a score on a short pass from Stafford to ensure that the drive to the red zone paid off.

But it wasn't enough to secure a Rams win.

In the end, the Rams didn't score enough points to beat an Arizona team that picked up its second win of the season. Now both teams are tied at the bottom of the NFC West at 2-4, well behind the 5-0 San Francisco 49ers, who play the Commanders on Monday Night Football. And the Cardinals have the edge in the standings thanks to the head-to-head win.

Making matters worse for the Rams, they leave the game with injury concerns on multiple fronts. All-Pro receiver Davante Adams came up limping on the game's final drive with what looked like a non-contact leg injury.

He did not return to the game. His status was unclear in the game's immediate aftermath.

And the Rams lost new kicker Blake Grupe to a knee injury in the first quarter, leaving them without a kicker and in precarious positions throughout the game. The Rams signed Grupe to replace Harrison Mevis, whom they cut after Monday's 37-34 loss to the Bills.

They went for two points and failed after a second-quarter touchdown to limit their lead to 9-6. They went for it on 4th-and-1 at the Arizona 27-yard line in the second half instead of attempting a game-tying 44-yard field goal. They failed to get the first down and turned the ball over on downs.

When they scored their late touchdown to tie the game at 15-15, punter Ethan Evans successfully kicked the extra point to momentarily give the Rams the lead.

The Rams have winnable upcoming games against Raiders, Chargers, Commanders and Cardinals again. But Sunday's game at home was also supposed to be winnable.

And while the loss was aided by a controversial penalty in the final seconds, it was poor play throughout the game from the Los Angeles offense that put the Rams in position to lose to begin with.

images.caption: Mathew Stafford was under pressure throughout Sunday's loss to the Cardinals. (AP Photo/Gregory Bull)

articles.title: Shane Steichen says Daniel Jones won't be benched but coach and general manager Chris Ballard are in trouble
articles.summary: Indianapolis Colts fans booed and chanted against Chris Ballard after a loss to the winless Tennessee Titans, putting Shane Steichen's job at risk.
articles.body: Head coach Shane Steichen was asked about his job status and whether quarterback Daniel is going to be benched, and it made sense because the Indianapolis Colts lost to the previously winless Tennessee Titans on Sunday. And let's cut to the chase: Steichen said Jones is not going to be benched despite throwing two interceptions to increase his season total to six in as many games. Jones has thrown at least one interception in each of the past four games. FROM THE CHARGERS TO THE COLTS AND FALCONS, WHICH OF THE NFL'S EIGHT WINLESS TEAMS ARE ALREADY IN PANIC MODE So Jones sticks for now. "I think Daniel knows he's got to play better," Steichen said. "I got to coach better." We all know by now that neither Steichen nor general manager Chris Ballard are likely to remain past the end of this season – assuming they even last that long – unless the club gets on a roll. That's how it is when the team has lost four of its six games, including two of three at home, and the home crowd booed lustily on Sunday afternoon. The boos metastasized to "fire Ballard" chants by game's end. Steichen understood the sentiment. "We've got to give them something to cheer about, you know?" he said. "I don't blame them for booing one freaking bit." The thing is, owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon seemed inclined to agree with fans' frustrations last season when she put everyone on blast. "I'm pissed. We're all pissed," she famously said after her team's 2025 collapse, consisting of seven consecutive losses to end the season. "We have been very clear with Chris and Shane that giving them another opportunity means that the sense of urgency for them to deliver and perform has never been higher. Chris and Shane are both capable of facing this challenge head-on and finding a way to achieve the results that our fans deserve, which is winning games, getting to the postseason and ultimately winning championships." So if that was the starting point, would Irsay-Gordon be likely to support her coach and GM now in the face of boos from her best customers? Nope. TITANS CEO APOLOGIZES TO BELEAGUERED FANBASE AFTER DREADFUL START TO THE SEASON: 'WE'RE SORRY' Losing to the Titans, who have struggled to merely keep their organizational flow chart straight the past three years, blew the pick of Malik Willis as their franchise quarterback, followed that by blowing the pick of Will Levis and are on track to blow the pick of Cam Ward, is embarrassing. So, of course, questions about Steichen's job status are fair. ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW! "Obviously, my job is to get this team ready and that's what I'm focused on right now," Steichen said. Steichen would be lucky to finish out the season barring a change of direction by his team. Such a move wouldn't necessarily fix things, but it would help give Irsay-Gordon a head start on a search for new people while avoiding the untidy approach of going behind her coach's back. articles.title: Kyren Williams Shades His Usage After Rams' Last-Second Loss to Cardinals
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Rams used two of their running backs nearly equally in Sunday's upset loss to the Arizona Cardinals, and at least one of them wasn't a fan of the game plan.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Rams used two of their running backs nearly equally in Sunday's upset loss to the Arizona Cardinals, and at least one of them wasn't a fan of the game plan.

After the loss, Kyren Williams said he should've been on the field more when asked why the Rams couldn't sustain energy across their offensive drives.

"Can't tell you, bro," Williams told reporters. "Probably because I'm not out there."

Williams was on the field far more than Blake Corum, but had 10 carries to Corum's nine. Williams rushed for 50 yards and added 17 yards through the air on three receptions, while Corum had 42 rushing yards and 18 receiving yards on two receptions, including a touchdown.

In the second half, the Rams turned it over on downs twice and fumbled once. They scored a late touchdown to go up 16-15, but the Cardinals won it on a last-second field goal.

While Williams has gotten far more carries than Corum this season, he seems to think head coach Sean McVay needs to prioritize putting him on the field more than Corum.

articles.title: 5 momentous plays in Week 6: 2 killer Jags penalties proved costly in loss to Texans
articles.summary: Two unfortunate Jaguars penalties and fumbles at critical junctures highlighted Sunday's most momentous plays.
articles.body:
In Week 5, the Jacksonville Jaguars were beneficiaries — and took advantage — of the Philadelphia Eagles' catastrophic late mistakes at Tottenham Hotspur.

On Sunday, on the other side of London, their luck changed with one bad-luck penalty … but they had no one to blame but themselves on another critical flag.

Fumbles were also at the forefront of Sunday's big momentum swings around the rest of the NFL, with three significant ones highlighted on our list.

Here were five plays that shifted Uncle Mo in considerable ways.

1. Phantom hold, 12-men penalties kill Jaguars' momentum

Two big plays loomed large in the Jaguars' 34-31 loss to the Texans in London . The first one was bad luck. The second was their own terrible mistake.

After the Texans took an early 7-0 lead on their second possession, the Jaguars marched right back down the field and appeared to level the game with a Bhayshul Tuten TD run. But the play was called back due to a questionable flag against Jacksonville's Brenton Strange. In what world is this holding?

The fact they couldn't come away with points on the drive made the poor call even more painful. Two plays later, Trevor Lawrence threw an end-zone interception to the Texans' Calen Bullock. Tuten later tied it midway through the second quarter, but that could have given the Jaguars a lead.

The bad call was bad luck. But several self-inflicted mistakes, including dropped passes, hurt the Jaguars further. One penalty was a real back breaker.

The Jaguars stopped the Texans, appearing to hold them to a three-and-out on Houston's first possession of the third quarter, with the Texans nursing a 17-14 lead. But on the punt, the Jags were flagged with having 12 men on the field, with Travis Hunter failing to get off the field in time.

It was an awful penalty, arguably their least excusable of the season. The Texans didn't mess around, marching all the way down for a touchdown.

Hunter had arguably his best NFL game , becoming just the third player since the NFL-AFL merger to catch a TD pass and intercept a pass in the same game. But his failure to get off the field on that third-quarter punt ended up being a huge momentum swing against his team.

Look at the stats from this game — basically dead even in many categories. This contest came down to a few unfortunate plays that went against the Jaguars, and they had control of one of them.

2. Henry's fumble was bigger than FG miss

Ravens kicker Tyler Loop missed a 49-yard field goal at the start of the fourth quarter in a 10-10 game, a big missed opportunity in what would end up a 13-10 Browns victory . However, the arguably more significant play came one series and a few game minutes later.

After the missed kick, the Ravens forced a quick three-and-out and got the ball back. After a Cleveland penalty, Derrick Henry appeared to be rumbling his way toward a first down on a first-and-5 run, but Browns linebacker Carson Schwesinger slashed into the fray and ripped the ball from Henry, which was recovered by the Browns' Tyson Campbell at the Baltimore 35-yard line.

A subsequent pass-interference call on the Ravens' Keyon Martin helped set up Audric Estime's tying touchdown and Cleveland's only TD of the game. The Ravens' offense had largely disappeared after the first quarter, and the Browns heated up just enough offensively to mount a final field-goal drive for the win.

Henry ran for 11 and 17 yards, respectively, on his first two carries of the game but was held to only 30 yards on his next 15 rushes. The fumble, however, was his biggest mistake, helping cost the Ravens a game they controlled by two scores.

"I told the team: 'Put this one on me,'" Henry said.

3. Kickoff strip fueled a 34-0 Saints run

The Saints found themselves in a 10-zip hole late in the second quarter against the Giants. Kicker Daniel Carlson's 58-yard bomb got them on the board with 1:09 left until halftime, but the Saints were not done scoring in the second quarter.

On the ensuing kickoff, the Saints' Isaiah Stalbird brilliantly forced a fumble on Giants returner Charlie Jones, which was recovered by Saints rookie Oscar Delp at New York's 28-yard line.

Tyler Shough then ripped off a 25-yard run to get New Orleans inside the 5-yard line, and Shough hit rookie Bryce Lance for a touchdown with one second left to tie it 10-10 at halftime.

That, and a 31-yard touchdown reception by Alvin Kamara to open the third quarter, comprised half of a 34-0 run by the Saints, flipping a 10-point deficit into a 24-point lead. And they'd need almost every one of those points, too, as J.J. McCarthy — replacing a benched Jameis Winston — led a furious Giants comeback that came up just short.

The Saints probably don't win without that massive swing before halftime.

4. Simmons' timely rip helps Titans win first

The Colts led 13-0 at halftime, unimpressively keeping the Titans at arm's distance while Tennessee's offense was stuck with the emergency brake still on. All signs pointed to an ugly Colts win, but they started giving the game away right after halftime.

On the Colts' first play from scrimmage, the Titans' Jeffery Simmons ripped the ball out from Jonathan Taylor, and the Titans recovered in business. It was just the jolt they needed.

The Titans used that gift to start chipping away at the deficit. They turned the recovery into a field goal and went on to outscore the Colts, 26-7, from that point on.

Cam Ward, who looked like he might be in danger of being benched at halftime, led five scoring drives in five second-half possessions, and the Titans returned a blocked punt for another touchdown.

The timing was tremendous for Ward and head coach Robert Saleh, who were both catching a lot of heat during the Titans' 0-5 start to the season. This win won't cool things off completely, but it was a much-needed victory. It all started with Simmons' game-changing forced fumble.

5. Cousins bombed away, but interception was a killer

The Raiders might have outscored the Bills in the first and fourth quarters, but the Bills won the middle portion of the game — and that's ultimately where Buffalo's 33-30 win was decided.

Tied at 13-all at the half, the Bills took the ball downfield quickly on their opening drive of the third quarter and appeared to score a TD, but it was wiped out by penalty. They settled for a field goal and a 16-13 lead that felt vastly different than a 20-13 advantage.

The Raiders played aggressively and looked very evenly matched at times with the Bills, but they were too aggressive on the ensuing drive after the field goal.

Kirk Cousins — who largely played very well — forced a pass into bracket coverage, and it was intercepted by the Bills' Dorian Williams. Cousins might have been fooled on the play, thinking Williams would continue following Brock Bowers, but Williams stayed inside on Michael Mayer, who was Cousins' target on the play.

Either way, the spacing on the routes felt crowded. You can't really blame the loss on Cousins. Without him, it's likely the Raiders can't keep pace with the Bills, even if they played a B or B- game on offense and were not lights-out good. It just happened to be an aggressive mistake by Cousins at a critical time while being fairly backed up on their own end of the field.

The Bills took advantage, even if the Raiders looked like they might hold them twice. Instead, a penalty gave them a first down after an incomplete pass, and Josh Allen made a circus TD pass to Keon Coleman.

The Raiders had a small margin for error, and Cousins' pick stung a little too deeply.

articles.title: Kansas City Chiefs star defensive lineman Chris Jones caught in screaming match with coaches on sidelines
articles.summary: Chris Jones shoved Chiefs coach Joe Cullen's hand away and ignited a screaming match on the Kansas City sideline during Sunday's win over the Chargers.
articles.body: The Kansas City Chiefs are once again heading towards yet another AFC West division title and likely Super Bowl win, but you'd never know it by how their sideline looked on Sunday. The Chiefs hosted the 0-5 Los Angeles Chargers at Arrowhead Stadium on Sunday afternoon, and the game pretty much went as expected. LA's hapless offense wasn't able to move the ball with any consistency and the Chiefs' offense imposed their will, outside two turnovers. JALEN HURTS CURSES AT RECEIVER IN VIRAL HOT-MIC MOMENT DURING EAGLES' COLLAPSE AGAINST RAMS With his team ahead 9-3 in the second quarter, Chris Jones, the Chiefs' star defensive tackle, sat down on the Kansas City bench. articles.title: Tyreek Hill’s $500,000 legal setback adds to comeback uncertainty as NFL insiders assess his signing prospects

articles.title: The Chiefs are 5-0 — and their offense may be returning to their dynastic heights
articles.summary: Kansas City remained undefeated this season with a 22-6 win over the Los Angeles Chargers.
articles.body: The Kansas City Chiefs your older sibling told you about may finally be back. The Chiefs improved to 5-0 with a 22-6 win over the Los Angeles Chargers on Sunday, and the Patrick Mahomes-led offense that once ran roughshod over the NFL appears to have returned in nearly full force. From 2018 (the year Mahomes became Kansas City’s starting quarterback) to 2022, the Chiefs ranked first in expected points added per play on offense over those five combined seasons, per RBSDM.com, a website that specializes in advanced analytics. In that time, Kansas City won two Super Bowls, while Mahomes won two regular-season MVP awards. From 2023 through 2025, however, the Chiefs ranked only 10th in offensive EPA, taking a significant step backward. Kansas City still managed to win one more championship during those three seasons. But in that time, the Chiefs also suffered a humiliating Super Bowl loss in which their offense crumbled, and last season they started 6-7 before Mahomes tore an ACL and ultimately missed the playoffs. Now, Mahomes and the Chiefs are undefeated through five games for only the third time in his career, and the offense much more closely resembles the heights of his torrid five-year start compared with the more recent three-season malaise. Entering Week 6, Kansas City ranked fourth in the NFL in EPA per play on offense, which would be its best finish since the 2022 campaign. The Chiefs also entered the week ranked second in EPA per rush, which would be their best mark this decade. There are several reasons for the offense’s stellar performance through five games. Mahomes himself has been better, posting his highest yards per attempt average and passer rating since 2022. Even after his no-touchdown, one-interception game against the Chargers, Mahomes is on pace to throw 32 touchdown passes this year, which would be his most since (you guessed it!) 2022. Meanwhile, Kansas City is also getting a major boost from running back Kenneth Walker III, who signed with the team before the season fresh off winning the Super Bowl MVP award with the Seattle Seahawks. Walker has rushed for at least one touchdown in every game but one so far this season. After having run for 128 yards and two scores against Los Angeles, Walker has amassed 655 yards and six touchdowns on the ground while adding two TDs as a receiver. “He’s a stud,” coach Andy Reid told reporters postgame. “He knows how to run the ball, knows how to set up runs. There’s an art to that and patience that you’ve got to have and vision and all those things that the great ones have. He’s got all of that, and he’s tough. He’s a tough kid.” Walker’s first five games have put him in elite company. He’s only the third player this millennium to have at least 750 scrimmage yards and eight touchdowns through the first five games of a season, according to NFL researcher Tony Holzman-Escareno. Priest Holmes did it in 2002 and won the Offensive Player of the Year award. Marshall Faulk did it in 2000 and won the same award ... as well as the MVP award. Walker is also the first player since Hall of Famer Jim Brown in 1963 with at least 600 rushing yards, six rushing touchdowns and multiple receiving touchdowns through his first five games, per Holzman-Escareno. The offense still may have another level to reach, according to Walker, who said postgame, “I feel like we’re going to get better.” (On top of all the offensive success, the Chiefs have also been stingy defensively, allowing only 16.3 points per game after Sunday’s win.) The last time Kansas City started 5-0 was in the 2024 season, when it finished the regular season 11-0 in one-score games and white-knuckled two playoff wins before getting blown out by the Philadelphia Eagles in the Super Bowl. But this is an entirely different 5-0, as the Chiefs are now powered by a highly efficient offense and a capable defense. While Kansas City has been a perennial title contender under Mahomes, this year’s team is much more formidable than it was the last few seasons. “We had played in so many Super Bowls, the last few we didn’t play our best in the regular season,” Mahomes said, saying coming back from the ACL injury has changed his perspective. “Today, for me, is about the process. Having to go through that rehab process and not play football has really made me enjoy the process of it.” He added, “You want to take advantage of every opportunity you get to step on the field.”

articles.title: Jim Harbaugh Talks Mike McDaniel's Future, Says Chargers Will 'Address Everything' After Chiefs Loss
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Chargers yet again struggled on the offensive side of the ball, managing just six points and 259 yards in a 23-6 loss against the Kansas City Chiefs on Sunday, a result that dropped them to 0-6.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Chargers yet again struggled on the offensive side of the ball, managing just six points and 259 yards in a 23-6 loss against the Kansas City Chiefs on Sunday, a result that dropped them to 0-6.

And yet again, head coach Jim Harbaugh found himself addressing the future of offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel and the play-calling duties.

"We're going to look at everything," he told reporters when asked if McDaniel would remain the play-caller. "The job I'm doing, it starts with me. The plan is we'll watch this and get with our offensive coaches. ... [Offense] Needs to be addressed."

"We have to address everything, guys, and especially offensively," he added. "We're not scoring enough points."

It was another brutal day for the team's offense, which also had two turnovers, gave up four sacks and was 0-for-3 on third down. The Chargers only rushed for 73 yards, far less than their average coming into the game (128.2 YPG), and remain one of the poorest passing offenses in football.

Something needs to change, and moving on from McDaniel feels more probable by the day. According to Mike Florio of Pro Football Talk, "There's a growing buzz that the Chargers will be [firing McDaniel], soon. Pass-game specialist Adam Gase, a former head coach of the New York Jets and Miami Dolphins, is expected to take over if McDaniel is fired."

The Chargers have undergone a shocking regression from last season's 11-6 record and postseason appearance. At this point, the playoffs aren't on anybody's mind in Los Angeles—getting a single win, and getting the offense back on track, remains the top priority.

articles.title: Fans question NFL's roughing-the-passer rules after controversial calls against Packers, Chiefs
articles.summary: Roughing the passer is increasingly proving to be a curse word among segments of the NFL fanbase.
articles.body:
Roughing-the-passer has always proved to be a sore subject for NFL fans. That fact resurfaced once more in Week 6.

Some might consider the penalty, ushered in to protect passers from sustaining major injuries, as a godsend. Others view it more negatively, believing it should be reformed to prevent honest defenders from coming under its wretched glare.

Regardless of where you stand on the debate, it's clear that many don't believe slight contact should come under its purview. Someone appeared to inform some of the NFL's referees, however.

NFL's roughing-the-passer rules come under fire after dubious calls against Packers, Chiefs

Quarterbacks live something of a charmed existence inside the pocket. Referees are often quick to blow a whistle if and when the gunslinger lands on their backside. While a great many of the collision that draw the umpire's glare are, indeed, excessive, there's a sentiment among NFL fans all roughing-the-passer calls aren't created equal.

During Week 6, the art of the new-age roughing-the-passer call was laid bare for all the wrong reasons. Calls against the Chiefs and Packers left some observers baffled.

Kansas City was the first to be felled by the call. Chris Roland-Wallace thought he had netted his first interception of the year in the the second quarter of Sunday's match. He nabbed a bouncing Justin Herbert pass after it leapt into and out of various sets of hands.

Roland-Wallace celebrated vociferously as he peered at his coup. He would soon be left dismayed when a canary flew from one referee's pocket. Ashton Gillotte was deemed to have roughed up Herbert on his pass attempt. A closer examination suggested that might have not been an accurate reading of the play.

Surely, Gillotte's unfortunate intervention would prove the only incident to ruffle football enthusiasts' feathers, right? Well, not exactly. Hours later, Lukas Van Ness was flagged after brushing Dak Prescott on a drop back.

Once more, the call proved significant. Prescott's subsequent toss landed in Carrington Valentine's hands for an interception. The referees' ruling rendered the takeaway null and void.

Neither call proved all that significant to shaping the final score. Both Kansas City and Green Bay emerged as victors, moving to 5-0 and 4-2, respectively. Still, the sight of seeing incidental contact punished so severely left masses of viewers with a bad taste in their mouths.

articles.title: College Football Playoff Expansion Leaves Broadcast Opportunities on the Sidelines
articles.summary: "Expanding the College Football Playoff to 24 teams will give more programs a chance to compete for a national championship. But the sport is missing a golde...
articles.body:
A handshake agreement. That's the term I saw all weekend regarding the College Football Playoff expanding from 12 teams to 24 beginning next year, with ESPN remaining the sole rights holder. There are positives and negatives to the reported deal, and it was refreshing to hear discourse on both sides of the argument across ESPN's networks this weekend. That's something college football fans didn't get with the network's coverage of the Protect College Sports Act.

However, in the end, ESPN owns all the goods. Again. The network has been the exclusive rights holder since the playoff began just 12 years ago. Fans can debate whether expanding the playoff to 24 teams will diminish the weekly must-win stakes of college football or lead to the elimination of conference championship games for major conferences. One thing remains clear: ESPN controls the entire package. That raises a question: If the sport wants to expand on the field, why can't it expand how those games are broadcast?

The old saying goes, "Follow the money." After signing a six-year, $7.8 billion exclusive extension in 2024, ESPN received an exclusive 30-day window to negotiate with the College Football Playoff over expansion. That window expired, but a handshake agreement was reportedly reached in the days that followed.

As a result, FOX Sports, CBS Sports/TNT Sports/Skydance, NBC Sports, and others never had an opportunity to compete for the expanded package during that window. Has ESPN dominated college football coverage for generations? Of course. Is watching College GameDay part of the average fan's Saturday routine during the fall? Absolutely.

But imagine if the NFL, MLB, NBA and NHL handled their biggest events the same way. Imagine if Kevin Burkhardt and Tom Brady were left out of the NFL's biggest games. What if Kenny Albert and Eddie Olczyk never got the opportunity to call the Stanley Cup Final?

That's the kind of opportunity the College Football Playoff could be taking away with this expansion. No Gus Johnson or Joel Klatt calling the sport's biggest games. No Brad Nessler and Charles Davis entertaining the audience.

Is that good for college football? No, it's not.

There are still specifics to work out. For instance, ESPN and TNT Sports have a sublicensing agreement that allows TNT Sports to broadcast select College Football Playoff games. That arrangement began in 2024 and currently runs through 2028. Now that Skydance owns both CBS Sports and TNT Sports, could those games move to CBS Sports beginning next year? Possibly. That could create an opportunity for Nessler and Davis to call a playoff game in the near future.

Regardless, what's puzzling about this deal is the question of inclusion. The expansion will affect conference championships and change the significance of regular-season losses. At the same time, it will give more teams a seat at the table by expanding access to the playoff.

More teams mean more games. So why not more networks? Why not give other television partners an opportunity to help grow the playoff by introducing it to different audiences and offering fans more broadcast options? Instead of allowing ESPN to control who gets what by arranging sub-license agreements. That doesn't benefit the playoff by only working alongside one broadcast partner.

ESPN is reportedly paying roughly $345 million more for the additional games on top of the approximately $1.3 billion it already pays each season. The network also recoups some of its investment through its sublicensing agreement with TNT Sports and could save money if several conference championship games are eliminated from its schedule.

If the additional rights cost $345 million for roughly six more games, did the College Football Playoff miss an opportunity to spark a bidding war? In all likelihood, would FOX, CBS/TNT/Skydance, CW, or NBC come to the table with more than that figure? More than likely yes, but we'll never know.

Don't get me wrong. ESPN delivers a quality college football product. I don't blame the network for paying for the right to negotiate first and taking advantage of that privilege. This isn't about ESPN. It's about the concept of inclusion if the playoff wants true expansion on all fronts.

Expanding the College Football Playoff to 24 teams will give more programs a chance to compete for a national championship. But the sport is missing a golden opportunity to expand something else just as important: the voices bringing those games to life. More teams and games should create more opportunities for the networks and broadcasters who have helped build the sport's popularity.

Instead, the College Football Playoff appears content to keep those broadcast opportunities largely within the same walls. I'm sorry, but inclusion shouldn't stop with the teams on the field.

If college football is willing to expand its playoff to give more programs a seat at the table, it should also be willing to broaden its broadcast partnerships. Doing so would give fans a wider selection of voices, perspectives and personalities calling the biggest games of the season.

The sport is expanding its postseason. It's time to expand the audience's experience with it.
