articles.title: ‘He is not human’ – NFL fans cannot believe Josh Allen’s ‘miracle play’ in big win
articles.summary: One Josh Allen masterclass moment has captured the attention of NFL fans after the Buffalo Bills’ big win and most are simply awestruck by his genius. In wha...
articles.body:
One Josh Allen masterclass moment has captured the attention of NFL fans after the Buffalo Bills' big win and most are simply awestruck by his genius.

In what proved to be a tight contest against the Las Vegas Raiders, the Buffalo Bills claimed their fifth win of the season. The difference-maker was none other than the team's star quarterback. Josh Allen did just enough to secure the victory for his team.

Allen threw the ball for 255 yards and two touchdowns, and looked like his usual impressive self during the game. The 33-30 scoreline suggests how tight the game was. And while a game like this is generally known for having a lot of big moments, one Allen play has really captured the fans' imaginations.

Josh Allen's third quarter scramble and touchdown pass left NFL fans online in awe of his skills

With the score at 16-13 in the third quarter, Allen had the ball for the Bills at the Raiders' 13-yard line. It was third down with eight yards to gain, and it would have been bad for Buffalo if they had to settle for the field goal.

The Raiders' defensive line knew they had to get the stop if they could. They sold out to try to sack Allen, but he somehow escaped the pocket. As more Las Vegas players rushed to meet him and put him on the ground, the 30-year-old casually flipped the ball to Keon Coleman in the endzone.

"Josh Allen is something else man, he is not human," one fan wrote. "Josh Allen is the 6th grader playing with 4th graders at recess," a second fan observed. "Josh Allen is not human. This is a new level of excellence we are not worthy of," said a third fan.

"I feel like even Josh Allen is surprised by the things Josh Allen can do sometimes," a fourth fan hilariously claimed. "Give him the MVP right now," a different comment read. "He can do anything. And his receivers know that at any moment he might do something nuts, so they're always ready. It's a pleasure to watch that man apply his craft," a sixth fan said.

The vision to see that play and the talent to make it are unfathomable for most quarterbacks, even at the highest level. Allen is making a strong case for himself to be named MVP for the second time in his career, and the fans clearly think he is the best around at the moment.

articles.title: J.J. McCarthy Sends Message to Giants Fans After Week 6 Outing
articles.summary: New York Giants quarterback J.J. McCarthy sent a message to the Giants fans following the team’s Week 6 loss to the New Orleans Saints.Despite being the home...
articles.body:
New York Giants quarterback J.J. McCarthy sent a message to the Giants fans following the team's Week 6 loss to the New Orleans Saints.

Despite being the home team, the Giants lost 34-27 to the Saints on Sunday. It was a tough game for New York, who took an early lead only to battle back from being down 24 points to make it close at the end, with a last-minute rally that ultimately fell short on a failed fourth-down play to seal the win for New Orleans.

Despite the tough loss, though, there are plenty of positives to take away from this game for Giants head coach John Harbaugh, including the strong play of McCarthy, who came off the bench in the second half of the game to take over for starting QB Jameis Winston and had a great showing in relief.

Despite the loss, McCarthy performed well, and the fans immediately took a liking to him, which he appreciated.

J.J. McCarthy Praises Giants Fans After Big Win

Speaking to reporters following the game, McCarthy praised the Giants fans for all of their support, showing how close the bond between the city and the player is already.

"I'm just extremely honored to be a part of the New York Football Giants, because this fanbase is unbelievable. The passion, how they show up every single game, home and away, it means the world to wear this blue and to play for them. All love to this city and the jersey, and I'm just extremely grateful for them," McCarthy said.

J.J. McCarthy Excelled Against New Orleans

Despite coming into the game in relief of a struggling Winston, McCarthy excelled during his first true opportunity to get reps for the Giants.

He was 11-for-23 in completions with 243 passing yards and one touchdown compared to one interception, and he gave the Giants a chance to win after being down big heading into the final quarter of the game, as it looked like New York was going to get blown out.

In the end, it was a loss for New York, which dropped their season record to 3-2-1, but it was still a really good showing by McCarthy, one that should give coach Harbaugh even more confidence to potentially start him going forward.

Although Harbaugh did not commit to giving McCarthy the start in the team's Week 7 game against the Houston Texans , he certainly needs to give it heavy consideration, given McCarthy's strong play in this game against the Saints and Winston's struggles overall behind center for the Giants this season.

Winston is an incredible teammate and someone whom the Giants love having around in the locker room, but he is more but he is much more suitable as a backup at this point in his NFL career.

McCarthy, meanwhile, was the 10th overall pick in the 2024 NFL Draft, and although it's been a struggle for him so far during his NFL career, he's still young enough to turn things around and show that he has what it takes to start games in this league.

articles.title: NFL Could Hand Down Punishment Over Rams Game After Controversial Call
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Rams could see the NFL take action following a polarizing decision against Josh Wallace in the loss to the Arizona Cardinals. The post NFL Co...
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Rams' loss to the Arizona Cardinals featured a polarizing call against cornerback Josh Wallace that could see the NFL step in.

Unfortunately for Wallace and the Rams, further discipline is among the possible outcomes.

On a first-and-10 play from the Cardinals 35-yard line, Arizona's Jacoby Brissett connected with wide receiver Jalen Brooks for a 21-yard gain. As he came down with the pass, Wallace was attempting to make the tackle, but connected with Brooks' helmet instead.

It was a blow from the shoulder. Officials still flagged Wallace for "unnecessary roughness," gifting the Cardinals 15 yards, putting them within field goal range.

There was also an offsides call against Josaiah Stewart, but the Cardinals, naturally, declined.

Rams' Josh Wallace Could Be Punished By NFL

During the game, rules analyst Mike Pereira sided with the broadcast team that the hit did not seem to meet the criteria for a flag, i.e. forcible contact to the head and or neck area. But Wallace must now be concerned that the NFL will side with the officials.

Wallace's hit could see the infraction specified as a "hit on a defenseless player." That is one of the NFL's fineable offenses.

Per the NFL , a first-time infraction can incur a fine as high as $17,911.

A second infraction could draw a fine as high as $23,882. This infraction would also count as one strike for Wallace. Two more strikes of this kind, and the third-year cornerback will trigger an automatic one-game suspension.

Wallace can appeal the fine, potentially leading to a reduction. However, the strike will carry over into future seasons if it holds.

To make matters worse, that was the only penalty called for a fineable offense in the game.

Wallace was also on the wrong side of a call against the Rams that altered their loss to the Denver Broncos in Week 3. He could see history repeat itself in that regard, but the Rams are feeling that in-game decision now.

"UNREAL PERSONAL FOUL," Sharp Football Analysis' Warren Sharp posted on X in reaction to the call, including a clip.

Rams On SI's Blaine Grisak posted , "How are we calling that unnecessary roughness on Josh Wallace?" adding that is was "another penalty this season late in the fourth quarter that Wallace has been screwed on."

"Another tough call on Josh Wallace there, and I don't love it, but the Rams put themselves in this position to lose this game," Sports Illustrated's Albert Breer posted on X.

Former NFL safety Quandre Diggs posted on X that the "Rams got cheated."

Rivals' Greg Biggins posted , "The League obviously hates Josh Wallace! What a wild way to lose a game [laughing face emoji]," underscoring the incredulous response to the call that many had in real time.

Wallace was playing so much partly due to the absence of Trent McDuffie. McDuffie suffered a groin injury in practice during the week.

Wallace will look to avoid the officials' attention in Week 7 against the Las Vegas Raiders .

articles.title: Jim Harbaugh to 'address everything' after latest loss drops Chargers to 0-6, leading to more Mike McDaniel questions
articles.summary: The Chargers "have to address everything, and especially offensively," Jim Harbaugh said on Sunday.
articles.body:
Calls for Mike McDaniels' job are only getting louder.

This time, though, Jim Harbaugh wasn't as strong in his defense of his offensive coordinator.

Harbaugh, after the Los Angeles Chargers fell 22-6 to the Kansas City Chiefs on Sunday, said that they are going to "have to address everything, and especially offensively." The loss knocked them to 0-6 on the season, which marks their worst start since 2000. Coincidentally, Harbaugh was on that Chargers team as a player that finished 1-15 that season.

And when asked about McDaniel directly and if he was going to keep calling plays, Harbaugh said they were "going to look at everything."

"The job I'm doing, it starts with me. We'll watch this and get with our offensive coaches," Harbaugh said, via ESPN . "I see the effort, I see the work being put in in the meetings, on the practice field, and to get that to translate to the field is what's necessary. Feel bad for our players, our team, our coaches, our fans. And [offense] needs to be addressed."

The Chargers only put up six points on Sunday, a season-low. They are averaging just 15 points per game, which is better than only the Miami Dolphins and Tennessee Titans. The Dolphins and Chargers are the only two teams in the league still without a win this season.

Justin Herbert went 22-of-37 for 204 yards with an interception. He was the team's leading rusher, too, with 26 yards. Herbert has thrown just five touchdowns to eight interceptions so far this season. He only threw 13 total interceptions last season in total.

"I don't know," Herbert said when asked what's not working for him offensively. "If I had the answers, then we'd definitely be having a different conversation."

It would take a truly historic turnaround for the Chargers to salvage this season and make the playoffs. Only one team has ever made the postseason after an 0-4 start — the Chargers did that in 1992 — but none has ever pulled that off after six straight losses.

Making a change at offensive coordinator, though, could be a first step. McDaniel is in his first season in the role after his split with the Miami Dolphins last season. He led that franchise for four seasons, and finished with just a 35-33 record.

NBC Sports' Mike Florio reported on Sunday that there is "growing buzz" that the Chargers will move on from McDaniel soon, too. When that happens, he said, former Dolphins and New York Jets head coach Adam Gase, now the Chargers' pass game specialist, would fill his role in the interim. The Chargers are entering their bye week, so it would leave them extra time to adjust to the change were they to make it now. But "soon," of course, is relative.

Simply firing McDaniel wouldn't cure everything, either. And Harbaugh isn't blaming him. They have a much bigger problem, and it starts at the top.

"There's no justification. Anything I would say would sound like an excuse. I'm opposed to that to the core and pointing fingers because I believe this is a team game," he said. "But definitely offensively, we need to evaluate and we need to look at it all — everything we're doing and how we're doing it."
